gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Everyone agreed the suggestion was utterly ___.
gaps.explanation: utterly ridiculous is the standard collocation; 'utterly' is used with extreme adjectives.

gaps.sentence: Shall we split it, or will you ___ the bill?
gaps.explanation: pay the bill is the fixed collocation in restaurants; 'spend the bill' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
The children ___ great fun at the fair.
Why don't we ___ lunch together on Friday?
gaps.explanation: have lunch is the standard collocation for eating lunch.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a look at that cut on your arm.
gaps.explanation: take a look (at something) is the fixed collocation for examining something briefly.
